summary_for_children: Al-Layl means The Night. It says people's efforts differ, and those who give and are mindful of Allah will find ease.
environment_concept: A courtyard split in two: one half tiled in deep blue with lanterns and night flowers for "the night when it covers" (92:1), the other in warm gold with sunflowers for "the day when it appears" (92:2). Beside it, a table set out for giving (92:5, 92:18). No person is shown. The Fire and the next life are not pictured.
architecture_and_scenery: A two-coloured tiled courtyard with lanterns on one side and sunflowers on the other, a giving table.

depiction_rules: No prophet, person or representation of Allah is shown. Unseen realities are never pictured. Interactive activities are labelled as adaptations.

unique_world.visual_theme: A tall village granary at nightfall with a hoist beam out from the loft and gifts for the poor waiting below

primary_mechanic.text: You can pull 25 kg; rig 1-4 pulleys so each load (20, 45, 70, 95 kg) hangs on enough strands to come within your strength, and no more (too few will not budge; too many pull needless rope and are refused) (92:5-7, easing toward ease; the pulleys are only a picture).

unique_world.narrative_structure: A reading under the oaks, the hoist, then a reading by the granary wall
environment_behaviour: each lifted gift waits in the loft door
unique_world.learning_objective: Know that Allah eases the giver toward ease (92:5-7)

story_library.source: Owner's 'Quran Adventure — Children's Story Library' (2026-11-04), first-draft narration for ages about 7-12
story_library.title: The Night and the Generous Heart
story_library.children_narration: Night and day are different, just as people's choices can be different. Surah Al-Layl contrasts generosity and mindfulness with selfishness. It reminds us that helping others sincerely is a meaningful way to live.

world_idea.title: The Two Paths
world_idea.description: Navigate a stylized day-and-night landscape and make age-appropriate choices about generosity and responsibility.

story_library.checks: Every reference exists in the verified text (checked 2026-11-04). Narration is draft, written by the owner, not reviewed by a scholar.
